architecture.summary: The tenant sweeps claim each daily tick in the tenant registry, so one instance of the control plane runs it: the SO-12 release rehearsal of 31 October 2026 measured that Render keeps the old instance for about 120 s after a new deploy is live, and a tick inside that time ran the organization sweep, the idle sweep, and the fleet summary in both instances, so Render could get a suspend or a delete two times and the summary line came two times. Inside the hosted Node server, the runner of tenants inserts the row of the tick (keyed by the tick time, with the claim holder of the sweeps, new at each start) into the new table thermus_admin.tenant_sweep_ticks before its steps, through a new statement of the fleet store on the sql runtime; only the instance whose insert adds the row runs the steps, the other writes one INFO line, and a claim without an answer runs no step and writes one ERROR line. App passes the fleet store and the holder to the runner and names the holder in the start line. The data contract of thermus_admin gains the table with SELECT and INSERT for the runtime role and forced row-level security (migration 20261101023017_tenant_sweep_ticks.sql, applied before the deploy). No component, container, public module, dependency, external call, or declaration snapshot changes. The selected C4 component view of the tenant registry changes (the label of tenants, the tick claims on the edge to sql, and the new table in PostgreSQL), the weekly sweep scenario gains the claim of the tick, and the idle sweep scenario names the claimed tick; the prose of the registry, the writers, the deployment view, the behavior section, and the known limits record the claim and the residual risk: when the old instance claims a tick and gets SIGTERM before its steps end, the rest of the tick waits until the next tick.
